review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no @[simp] declarations and no simp-set manipulation, so there are no competing rules, rewrite cycles or bad orientations to report. The only candidate for a simp lemma is `star_exp_ofReal_mul_I_eq_inv`, a `star (exp (t*I)) = (exp (t*I))⁻¹` rewrite. It is used in one `rw` and one local `simp only [...]` call. Its right-hand side `(exp (t*I))⁻¹` is not obviously a better normal form than `star (exp ..)`. It would also clash with existing `Complex.exp_conj` and `star_def` rewrites. The call sites already pass it explicitly, so I did not find enough support to recommend a global attribute. I grepped Mathlib for existing simp lemmas about `conj (exp ..)` or `star (exp ..)` and found nothing that makes it redundant, but also nothing that justifies promoting it. The other lemmas are bespoke helper facts, and the many `simp_all` and `simp [...]` calls are proof-style choices rather than simp-interface defects. I could not run Lean, so I make no claim about observed simp behaviour.
